events.title: Telegram
events.text:
A Houthi ballistic missile strike on a Saudi-run training base in Yemen's Shabwah province on Oct. 19 killed at least 75 people and wounded more than 200, Saudi troops among them.
Saudi and Yemeni officials briefed on the attack say it was the deadliest single Houthi strike of the new war. 
Three missiles hit the al-Alam camp within a few minutes, just as Saudi officers were starting a training session for newly enlisted local forces. 
Witnesses said four battalions had gathered when the first missile hit, and one of the later missiles struck recruits as they ran from the first blast. 
Drones had been circling the base for days beforehand. 
Relatives of the dead and wounded blamed the local Yemeni commander for ignoring those warnings. 
Officials said the camp had no air-defense or early-warning systems, and Shabwah authorities are now pressing Riyadh to supply them quickly.

Ukrainian drones struck Russia’s Voronezh overnight on October 26, triggering fires and explosions across the city.
Russian military correspondents described it as one of the most intense drone attacks on the city since the war began.
The Voronezhsintezkauchuk synthetic rubber plant was reportedly targeted, while a drone also struck a business center.
Two people were reported killed and 17 injured.

🇺🇸🇰🇷US bets on South Korea to revive its ailing shipbuilding industry
[US Navy shipbuilding](https://t.me/geopolitics_prime/69431) is mired in a systemic crisis, with America producing less than 1% of the world’s ships while [China boasts ](https://t.me/geopolitics_prime/74689)over 230 times its shipbuilding capacity.
China is expected to capture more than three-quarters of new commercial orders by tonnage this year. 
South Korea, a distant second with roughly 16% of orders, has emerged as the US’ key partner in an effort to reverse the atrophy as [Trump pushes](https://t.me/geopolitics_prime/74689) for a “Golden Fleet,” reports the WSJ.
🔴 Hanwha Ocean has invested around $350M in Philadelphia’s shipyard since acquiring it in 2024; it aims to certify the facility for combatant shipbuilding by 2028
🔴 Hanwha was recently selected to build a specialized auxiliary vessel for Trump’s Golden Dome missile-defense system 
🔴 South Korea has pledged $150B toward US shipbuilding under its trade deal with Trump
🔴 HD Hyundai and US construction firm Kiewit have formed a joint venture to develop an advanced American shipyard (full operations targeted for 2029)
US law requires naval ships to be built domestically, but in the scramble to revive its shipbuilding, the White House wants to allow foreign shipyards to build a limited number abroad if they make substantial investments in the US.
